stories.researchAngle: Extend the methodology to vehicles not covered, or correlate discovered endpoints with known API vulnerability classes (VIN-based authorization, IDOR) under a bug bounty scope.
stories.summary: A US academic team monitored the Wi-Fi and cellular traffic of 21 modern cars to map every endpoint they talk to. Most payloads were encrypted, but the domain maps and third-party services they uncovered are detailed. The paper is titled “Automatic Transmission: An Empirical Study of Data Privacy in the Connected Vehicle Ecosystem.”
stories.title: Researchers capture and analyze network traffic from 21 connected vehicles
stories.whyItMatters: It’s effectively a published attack-surface map of OEM backends and third-party telemetry partners, which is where the biggest recent car breaches have come from.

stories.title: Oil, debt and the coming reset in car values – and what it means for EVs - The Driven
stories.summary: Oil, debt and the coming reset in car values – and what it means for EVs The Driven

stories.researchAngle: Study how dealer and service portals authenticate to OEM telematics backends and what a stolen dealer credential can do to a car.
stories.summary: A German dealer software platform was accessed for about three weeks by an intruder using credentials it already held, with deal and financing data copied. Separately, Ivanti disclosed on Oct. 13 that a Connect Secure VPN flaw (CVE-2026-104935) was being exploited, and CISA added it to its KEV catalog the same day.
stories.title: German dealer software platform breached for three weeks; Ivanti VPN zero-day exploited
stories.whyItMatters: Dealer platforms often hold privileged access to vehicle activation and owner accounts, so a dealer compromise can become a vehicle compromise.

stories.researchAngle: Build a public dataset that classifies incidents by attack surface over time and test whether the shift holds across Upstream, PCA, and VicOne data.
stories.summary: VicOne’s Q3 2026 situational awareness report counted about 400 automotive cyber incidents and found that in-vehicle systems were affected more than enterprise IT for the quarter.
stories.title: VicOne Q3 report: in-vehicle systems overtake enterprise IT as the most-hit target
stories.whyItMatters: Most automotive incidents have historically been ordinary IT breaches at OEMs and suppliers. A shift toward the vehicle itself signals attackers getting closer to cyber-physical impact.

stories.researchAngle: Aftermarket units make great lab targets. Buy one, audit the patched vs. unpatched firmware, and measure how many installed units ever receive the update.
stories.summary: Sony fixed seven vulnerabilities in its XAV-9500ES aftermarket head unit that could have allowed device compromise through wireless and USB interfaces. VicOne published an attack-path walkthrough.
stories.title: Sony patches seven XAV-9500ES head unit flaws over Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and USB
stories.whyItMatters: Aftermarket head units are cheap, widely installed, rarely updated, and often bridged to the car’s CAN bus.

stories.researchAngle: Reproduce the attack in CARLA or another simulator and test whether cross-sensor consistency checks or temporal plausibility checks catch it.
stories.summary: TUM researchers are studying how attacks on optical sensors can deceive autonomous vehicles and how cars could respond on their own. Their paper on a new LiDAR-and-camera attack vector is set for USENIX VehicleSec ’26 in Baltimore, alongside an ASIA CCS SoK on camera image-pipeline security.
stories.title: TUM shows “perspective-shift” attacks that fool LiDAR and cameras at once
stories.whyItMatters: Attacks that defeat both LiDAR and camera undercut the main assumption behind sensor fusion as a defense.

stories.researchAngle: With an SDR and an open-source LTE stack in a shielded enclosure, test whether other OEMs’ telematics units show the same fallback and SMS handling weaknesses.
stories.summary: Researchers tested the LTE connectivity of two production Teslas and demonstrated IMSI catching, attaching to and hijacking via a rogue base station, insecure fallback behavior, silent SMS injection, and spoofed broadcast messages.
stories.title: WOOT ’26 paper: rogue base stations, IMSI catching, and silent SMS against Tesla Model 3 and Cybertruck
stories.whyItMatters: The cellular modem is a car’s most exposed remote interface. This is hands-on proof against real production vehicles, not a simulation.

stories.researchAngle: Survey BLE commissioning interfaces across commercial chargers for the same pattern: unauthenticated GATT services that touch firmware or config.
stories.summary: Per the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, the charger’s Bluetooth interface let an unauthenticated attacker pull sensitive data, reboot the station, and submit a firmware-update URL. It’s scored CVSS v4.0 8.7 (High).
stories.title: CVE-2026-22099: EVbee DC fast charger Bluetooth interface had no authentication
stories.whyItMatters: An attacker-supplied firmware URL over unauthenticated Bluetooth is a short path to persistent charger takeover, and chargers talk to both vehicles and the grid.

stories.researchAngle: Run a comparative teardown of infotainment-to-body-control isolation across brands and countries of origin.
stories.summary: Following an ABC report, a security expert gained control of a BYD Shark 6’s locks, headlights, and audio and video systems and said it was easier than expected. The article also recaps Tesla cellular research, QNX attacks, and Nissan Leaf Bluetooth exploits.
stories.title: Researcher takes over BYD Shark 6 locks, lights, and media with surprising ease
stories.whyItMatters: It feeds the policy debate on Chinese-made vehicles while showing that the weaknesses are industry-wide, not tied to one country.

stories.researchAngle: Diff firmware 1.9.1 against earlier releases to study patch completeness and look for variant bugs.
stories.summary: Phoenix Contact fixed 20 vulnerabilities in its CHARX SEC-3xxx charge controllers in firmware 1.9.1. VicOne explains how they could have given deeper control of chargers.
stories.title: Phoenix Contact patches 20 CHARX SEC-3xxx EV charger controller vulnerabilities
stories.whyItMatters: CHARX has been a repeat Pwn2Own Automotive target, which shows that charge controllers keep yielding chained bugs.

stories.researchAngle: Collect cheap Android head units, monitor their update channels and network traffic, and build detection signatures for proxy behavior.
stories.summary: Kaspersky documented what it calls the first campaign built specifically for vehicle head units: malware pushed through trusted Android software updates, pulling devices into a botnet linked to residential proxy services.
stories.title: Kaspersky finds BadBox-linked malware delivered to Android car head units via updates
stories.whyItMatters: Car head units are being turned into proxy nodes. That’s a monetization model, so expect more of it.

stories.researchAngle: Use the taxonomy to find which quadrants have the fewest defense papers relative to attack papers.
stories.summary: A comprehensive survey sorts vehicle attacks and defenses into four tracks: body and physical systems, access and engine start, electronic and software systems, and ADAS and autonomous driving.
stories.title: New survey: from mechanical lock-picking to autonomous driving deception
stories.whyItMatters: It’s not news itself, but it’s a strong map of the field for finding under-studied gaps.

stories.researchAngle: Buy used infotainment units from salvage marketplaces and quantify how much previous-owner data survives a factory reset.
stories.summary: PCA counted 345 automotive-specific vulnerabilities in Q2, up 30% from Q1, with high-severity findings more than doubling. Highlights include cloud auth weaknesses in shared EV chargers, e-bikes, and e-scooters, ransomware against a UK vehicle-valuation provider, and unencrypted owner data left on second-hand infotainment systems.
stories.title: PCA Q2 2026: 345 automotive vulnerabilities, 161 high severity, 94% low complexity
stories.whyItMatters: Nearly all the bugs needed low attack complexity, which means the barrier to exploitation is low.

stories.researchAngle: Inventory dealer-installed telematics add-ons sold in the US and assess their BLE pairing and authentication.
stories.summary: A device sold to dealerships as an anti-theft tool turned out to let an attacker connect over Bluetooth and unlock doors, honk, and flash lights on at least two million Honda, Toyota, Jeep, and other vehicles. It doesn’t start the engine. The vendor called real-world risk low; a UCSD professor called it possibly the worst car-hacking threat he had seen.
stories.title: UCSD researchers find Bluetooth flaw in dealer anti-theft device on ~2M vehicles
stories.whyItMatters: Dealer-installed aftermarket telematics sits outside OEM security programs and is nearly invisible to owners.

stories.researchAngle: Develop SBOM-based methods to verify software provenance in telematics units, which is the technical problem the rule leaves to industry.
stories.summary: In June 2026 the Commerce Department denied Polestar authorization to sell model-year 2027 vehicles in the US under the Connected Vehicle Rule. The rule bars Chinese- or Russian-linked software from MY2027 and connectivity hardware from MY2030.
stories.title: Connected Vehicle Rule bites: Commerce denies Polestar MY2027 US sales authorization
stories.whyItMatters: Ownership alone, not just where the car is built, can trigger exclusion. That reshapes software supply chains and the vehicles available to test.

stories.researchAngle: Explore detection by sampling and differential-testing subnetworks, or provenance attestation for model weights in the AV build pipeline.
stories.summary: Researchers showed a backdoor that hides in one subnetwork of the weight-sharing super networks used in autonomous driving. It stays dormant until that configuration is selected, then hijacks behavior with near-certain success, and current tools can’t practically detect it.
stories.title: VillainNet: a near-undetectable backdoor hidden in AV “super network” AI models
stories.whyItMatters: Supply-chain attacks on ML models are the AV equivalent of firmware backdoors, and model provenance is barely regulated.

stories.researchAngle: Model how ransomware at a telematics provider propagates to fleet-level vehicle availability (the Q1 2026 bricking incident is a case study).
stories.summary: Upstream analyzed 494 publicly reported 2025 incidents. Ransomware made up 44% and is spreading from IT into vehicles on the road, while APIs, cloud backends, and AI systems are the fastest-growing weak points.
stories.title: Upstream 2026 report: automotive ransomware more than doubles, and AI expands the attack surface
stories.whyItMatters: It’s the industry’s most-cited annual baseline and shapes OEM budgets and regulatory talking points.
